plan.topic: Barely hungry on tirzepatide: making a small plate still bring fibre, without making the stomach worse
plan.angle: Sentence 1 as written. Label fact on its own: tirzepatide reduces appetite and food intake (label wording). Optional hook, only if verified: 'A UK review found little research on diet quality during these medicines. One study it covered reported low fibre intake. That's early evidence, not proof.' Otherwise skip the hook and go straight to habits. Advisory habits at their exact wording: build fibre up gradually and pair it with fluids, unless you've been told to limit fluids. Untagged idea: add one fibre food you already like to the small plate you eat (beans, berries, oats, vegetables). Suggest asking about a dietitian. No grams, calories, supplements or 'bad' foods. Then 'Not personal advice, so ask your prescriber.' and the loop line.
plan.working_title: Tirzepatide: Eating Less, Getting Enough Fibre? #shorts
plan.why: A fresh practical-moment angle on our second-best long-form topic (What to Eat). It uses this week's nutrition coverage only as evidence, never as the topic, and keeps the 13:00 slot off news. | fact-check: A useful, safe angle that stays clear of restrictive eating. I couldn't find the 'small UK study of 14 people on GLP-1 medicines'. The closest verifiable UK source is a Cambridge/UCL review in Obesity Reviews. It found only 12 studies on diet alongside semaglutide or tirzepatide, and reported fibre intake about half the recommended amount in one study. Don't use an unverified n=14 study as the hook. Either find the primary paper and confirm its sample, design and finding, or use the review with a hedge, or drop the study line. Quote the 2025 joint advisory word for word, and keep its 'first few days' nausea note at that exact scope. Don't attach the label's appetite wording to fibre advice. No grams target, because a number can read as a nutrition prescription. Keep 'unless you've been told to limit fluids' word for word. Add 'If fibre makes your stomach worse, tell your prescriber.'

package.title: Tirzepatide and a Tiny Plate: Fibre Still Matters #shorts
package.description:
Barely hungry on tirzepatide doesn't mean fibre stops mattering. Add one fibre food you already like, build it up gradually and pair it with fluids, unless you've been told to limit fluids.
Severe stomach pain that won't go away needs medical help right away. For anything that isn't one of those emergency signs, don't stop or change your medicine on your own.
#tirzepatide
Not personal advice. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

factcheck.summary:
The Short is accurate and safe. It comes to about 109 spoken words, which is inside the tight arm (90–120) and well under the 160-word cap. I found two minor issues and no factual errors.

**What I checked against the sources:**
- **s3 (label fact):** the live Zepbound HTML label (revised 8/2026), Section 12.2, says word for word: "Tirzepatide decreases calorie intake. The effects are likely mediated by affecting appetite." The script keeps the "likely" hedge. It shows this as a label fact and doesn't tie it to the fibre advice.
- **s5 (fibre advice):** the 2025 joint advisory from ACLM, ASN, OMA and TOS (Am J Clin Nutr 2025;122(1):344–367, PMID 40450457, full text on PMC) supports it. The advisory encourages "adequate fluids and fiber from foods" and "a gradual increase in foods with soluble and insoluble fiber". It says this in the section on managing constipation during GLP-1 therapy for obesity. The script's general advice to build fibre up slowly with fluids stays within that.
- **Fluids line:** the "unless you've been told to limit fluids" exception is spoken and shown on screen.
- **Food list (s4):** the foods are ordinary examples with no source tag, which is correct for our own tips.

**Safety and closing:**
- s6 sends people to their prescriber or a dietitian if fibre upsets their stomach.
- The closing safety line is exact and appears as one card that ends on a full stop.
- There is no subscribe line or "link in the description".
- Nothing nudges people to eat less, gives doses, or talks about stopping the medicine.

**Minor issues (fixes listed below):**
- The s5 caption ends on a full stop while the other content cards don't.
- s6 doesn't say what to do about severe or persistent stomach pain. I suggest adding a clause to its narration.

The Thanksgiving watch-next target named in s8's post note isn't on the playbook's linking list. That's for the publisher to settle and isn't a content error.

issues.claim: If fibre makes your stomach worse, tell your prescriber.
issues.problem: The line covers ordinary discomfort but doesn't say what to do about severe or lasting stomach pain. On tirzepatide that pain can signal something urgent, such as pancreatitis. A viewer could just wait for their next appointment. This isn't wrong, just incomplete.
issues.fix: Narration: "If fibre makes your stomach worse, tell your prescriber. Severe stomach pain that won't go away needs medical help right away. And ask whether a dietitian could help with small plates." On-screen text: "Stomach worse? Tell your prescriber. Severe pain? Get help right away." (This adds 10 words, for about 119 in total, still inside the tight arm.) If you add the emergency line, follow it with the fixed don't-stop line as the rules require, or keep the original s6 and accept the gap.

issues.claim: Build up slowly with fluids (unless told to limit fluids).
issues.problem: The punctuation doesn't match the other content cards: this is the only one apart from the closing lines that ends on a full stop. It's wording polish only.
issues.fix: Change the on-screen text to: "Build up slowly with fluids, unless told to limit fluids". Keep it as one card and don't split it at the comma.
